newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour surge threatens government whip's seat.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour surge threatens government whip's seat.

text.p: Roger Sowry, the National Government's senior whip, is in danger or losing his seat, according to a poll taken in the Otaki electorate which shows a strong surge in support for the main opposition Labour Party.
The poll, published in Friday's Evening Post newspaper, shows Labour's Judy Keall with 46 percent of the vote, ten points ahead of Sowry and up 11 points on her rating in a similar poll in July.
In the party vote, which will determine the overall make-up of parliament after the October 12 election, Labour had narrowed the gap between it and the ruling National Party.
In July National was attracting 39 percent against 21 percent for Labour. But in Friday's poll Labour was on 28 percent against 35 percent for National.
The other two main opposition parties, the left wing Alliance and economic nationalist New Zealand First, polled 16 percent and 13 percent respectively.
That marks a six point rise for the Alliance and an eight point fall for NZ First since the July poll.
Both Sowry and Keall played down the poll saying their own soundings had the race much closer.
The poll of 900 voters was taken last weekend.
